title: A frog with horns in the Late Cretaceous: new information on Hungarobatrachus szukacsi (Neobatrachia: Anura)
content:
Abstract
The Late Cretaceous Hungarobatrachus szukacsi from Hungary is the only Mesozoic neobatrachian species known in Laurasia. Previously represented by isolated and incomplete ilia (including the holotype), tibio-fibulae, maxillae, squamosals, angulosplenials, and frontoparietals, Hungarobatrachus szukacsi has been regarded as a possible ranoid or hyloid. A recently discovered, three-dimensional skull of Hungarobatrachus szukacsi preserves the paired otoccipitals and squamosals, an incomplete left pterygoid, and posterior portions of the parasphenoid and fused frontoparietals in articulation. The new skull shows an unexpected and rare feature: the dorsal, posterolateral corners bear a horn-like paraoccipital process formed by a posterior elongation of the processus posterdorsalis and processus dorsalis of the squamosal. Elsewhere among anurans, paraoccipital processes occur in just two other neobatrachian genera (all species of Hemiphracus and several species of Ceratophrys), but the composition and form of paraoccipital processes differ among the three taxa. Our new cladistic analyses suggest that Hungarobatrachus szukacsi and four other Late Cretaceous neobatrachian species, two each from South America and Africa, may be australobatrachians, yet are not members of either the less inclusive Calyptocephalellidae or Myobatrachoidea. If correct, this result indicates that australobatrachians were more diverse and widely distributed during the Late Cretaceous than previously recognized.
